script: [serious] 1912. An amateur archaeologist named Charles Dawson announces the find of the century. Near Piltdown, in England, he's found a skull... and a jaw. Proof, experts said, of the missing link between apes and humans. The Natural History Museum backed him. It was named Dawson's Dawn Man. For forty years, it was in the textbooks. More than two hundred and fifty papers were written about it. Then, in 1953, scientists ran a new chemical test. [whispers] The skull and the jaw were from different times... and different species. The skull was a medieval human's. The jaw, an orangutan's. The teeth had been filed down by hand and stained to look ancient. Under a microscope, you could see the file marks. And Dawson? A historian later documented at least thirty-eight other fakes linked to him. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number eight. Which file should we open next?
